grid.doc: container width x height = 10 x 7: the wall itself. index = row * 10 + column, row 0 the top row, column 0 the left as seen from the front.

space.unity: prefab space, origin on the floor at the centre of the footprint (the runners), +z front, +y up, +x to the furniture's left when seen from the front

frame.size_doc: width (x) x depth incl. the runners (y) x height (z). Width = 10 x 0.375 m: half-pitch ends, two side by side continue the board grid. The back is flat: every part is at or in front of the back plane (Unity z = -0.25), so the piece stands flush against a wall; the 0.50 m runners run forward only. Trophies reach the runner tips (0.34 m in front of the board face).

fill_order: grid order, mirroring the 10 x 7 container grid: index = grid_row * 10 + grid_col; rows top to bottom, each row left to right seen from the front. Every row has its own height, so rows of 10 by position.y descending, each by position.x descending, give the same order.
position: unit position = the hang point: the centre of the board's FRONT face. box_size = the fit box [x width, y height, z depth] in Unity axes.
copy_rule: After item_rotation, s=min(max(DisplaySize*RootScale,0.23/max(turnedBounds.x,turnedBounds.y)),1.15*min(box/turnedBounds)). Keep original back anchor and cell cap. One actual representative per inventory stack, empty board stays empty. NEW in the 10 x 7 variant: copies[0].rotation per place is a small hand-hung turn (Unity euler x pitch +-0.8, y yaw +-1.0, z roll = the plaque's own roll +-0.6 plus +-0.4 deg; neighbours never alike), applied after item_rotation (r = c.Rot * align, already in Storehouse.cs). The fit uses the item turn only, so the amplitudes are sized for r3's place box: that box (0.363 x 0.2605 x 0.322) turned by them stays clear of its neighbours' boxes and of the plaque's iron; measured again on the real meshes.
item_rotation_doc: NEW in r2. Top-level, per trophy prefab name, Unity euler degrees (Quaternion.Euler) of the mounting turn: the item turned about its bounds centre BEFORE Aligned and the copy's rotation, so the face (or muzzle) looks out of the wall (+z) and ~15 degrees down. 0 = as ripped (the game's models lie face up, so most heads need x 15..105). A kind missing from the table is unturned.

placement.anchor_back: NEW. 'anchor': 'back' = the item's bounds hang on the unit's plane instead of standing on it. In Storehouse.cs: StoreCopy gets 'public bool Back;'; Copy(): 'if (S(cd, "anchor") is { } anchor) { c.Bottom = anchor.StartsWith("bottom", StringComparison.Ordinal); c.Back = anchor.StartsWith("back", StringComparison.Ordinal); }'; Place(): after 'if (c.Bottom) centre.y += s * d.y * 0.5f;' add 'if (c.Back) centre.z += s * d.z * 0.5f;'. Nothing else changes (offset.z then adds the 18 mm clearance).
placement.without_it: Without the change the trophy is centred on the hang point, half its depth inside the board (up to 0.16 m): the file still loads, it just looks sunk.
placement.kind: board (every unit): display store, mirror = true, container 10 x 7, one trophy per stack; the stack count does not matter (one model per stack).
placement.demo: example_item / example_scale per unit = the trophy in the full render: Joost's 65 non-boss kinds by biome (bosses are refused), then repeats of common heads.
placement.item_rotation: NEW in r2, Storehouse.cs, 4 small edits. (1) StoreUnit: 'public Dictionary<string, Quaternion> ItemRot;'. (2) ItemVisual: 'public string PrefabName => prefabName;'. (3) Anchors.Parse: before the unit loop 'var itemRot = ItemRotations(doc);', in the StoreUnit initializer 'ItemRot = itemRot,', and the helper 'static Dictionary<string, Quaternion> ItemRotations(Dictionary<string, object> doc) { if (Json.Obj(doc, "item_rotation") is not { } t) return null; var d = new Dictionary<string, Quaternion>(); foreach (var kv in t) if (V(t, kv.Key) is { } e) d[kv.Key] = Quaternion.Euler(e); return d; }'. (4) StoreModel.Place: right after 'var align = Aligned(c, size);' add 'if (u.ItemRot != null && item.PrefabName != null && u.ItemRot.TryGetValue(item.PrefabName, out var turn)) align *= turn;'. Nothing else: r = c.Rot * align and d = Turned(align, size) then include the item turn, so the fit box, the 'back' anchor and the turn about the bounds centre follow by themselves.

note: Trophy Hall 10 x 7 r1 (Claude Opus 5.5, 25 Oct 2026; Joost 25 Oct 19:2x: 'add both' sizes for his 65 non-boss trophies, on the wall or on the floor): r3's boards, pitch, fit box, hang clearance, atlas and item_rotation unchanged; new frame: flat back (stud frame behind a plank skin, runners forward only), half-pitch ends with half-width end posts, runners and straps (two units tile without a seam), 2 bays. 70 places for 65 kinds: 5 stay empty until more trophies exist.

checks.doc: every ripped trophy (71 kinds), turned by item_rotation and its place's copy rotation and placed by the mod rule on EVERY board (4970 placements per rule), against the whole frame (BVH overlap of the real triangles): clip pairs r3 rule 0, runtime rule 0, cap rule (1.15 x fit, the largest any rule gives) 0. Worst clearance between two neighbours for any pair of kinds (r3 rule): 8.4 mm sideways, 9.5 mm up/down. coplanar_frame: see zaudit (independent check).

kinds_missing.TrophyForestTroll: no mesh in the game bundle (null MeshFilter mesh); the mod measures the real prefab at run time, the fit rule is the same. Its item_rotation entry [20, 0, 0] is copied from TrophyFrostTroll (same troll head model family) and NOT verified on a mesh.
